decision: Schedule knobs: GEMV token tile {1,8,16,32,64} (template) and simdgroups per threadgroup {1,2,4,8} (runtime), separately for decode (M=1) and narrow prefill (M>1, N<=64); GEMM tile among the 8 compiled shapes, one tile for every M>1; MoE tiled (BN, rows, K step) in {32,64}x{16,32,64}x{16,32} minus 64x64 (threadgroup memory); MoE row-kernel simdgroups {2,4,8,16}; attention key split {4,8,16} with dynamic threadgroup memory, separately for decode and prefill; GDN parts {1,2,4,8}, separately for decode and prefill
why: array sizes need templates, dispatch shapes can be runtime parameters without recompiling; the M=1 versus M>1 split keeps the prefix-cache invariant that a row's result is the same in any chunk of 2 or more rows

decision: Measurement: per entry a workload on real resident weights rotated over 10 layers, 5 interleaved rounds, median per candidate, 60 s budget; prefill entries time a 128-row and a 32-row chunk together so the one GEMM tile is not chosen for 128 rows alone; a candidate replaces the default only when it validates at 1e-5 relative L2 against the default's output on the same inputs and is at least 2 percent faster
why: the audit of the previous run found day-to-day drift of about 10 percent and kbench repeats within 2 percent at best, so a smaller gain is noise and changing summation order for noise is not worth it
